The story begins with the introduction of the Dashwood family, who have lived at Norland Park in Sussex for many generations. The old gentleman grew attached to his nephew's family, including his three daughters, and intended to leave the estate to them.

However, when the old gentleman dies, his will is read, and it is discovered that he has left the estate to his great-nephew, a four-year-old boy, with the condition that it cannot be sold or used to provide for Mr. Dashwood's daughters. Mr. Dashwood is disappointed, but his temper is cheerful, and he hopes to live for many years and save enough money to provide for his family.

Tragically, Mr. Dashwood dies just a year later, leaving his widow and daughters with only £10,000, including the £1,000 each that the old gentleman had left to the girls. Before his death, Mr. Dashwood asks his son, John Dashwood, to look after the interests of his stepmother and half-sisters, but it is unclear whether John will fulfill this request. The chapter sets the stage for the rest of the novel, which will follow the lives of the Dashwood sisters, Elinor and Marianne, as they navigate love, heartbreak, and financial uncertainty.
